title: When the Interpreter Asked a Question
title_ja: 通訳者が質問したとき
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、制度、実証結果ではない。登録台帳は制作来歴確認用。

sentences.en: At an imagined international youth conference, a team of students was given the responsibility of translating a discussion between participants who shared an interest in environmental projects but did not share a common first language.
sentences.ja: 架空の国際青少年会議で環境活動への関心は共通だが母語が異なる参加者間の議論を通訳する責任を学生チームが担った。

sentences.en: The organizers expected the interpreters to transfer each speaker's statements into another language as accurately and efficiently as possible, so that the participants could continue discussing their proposals without lengthy interruptions.
sentences.ja: 主催者は議論を長く中断せず続けられるよう各発言をできる限り正確かつ効率的に別言語へ移すことを期待した。

sentences.en: During one discussion, a participant suggested that the group should make a particular activity compulsory for everyone who registered, using an expression whose intended strength was not entirely clear to the interpreter.
sentences.ja: ある議論で参加者は登録者全員に特定活動を必須にする案を述べたが、その表現の意図した強さは通訳者に完全には明らかでなかった。

sentences.en: The interpreter hesitated because translating the expression as an obligation rather than a strong recommendation might substantially alter the response of the people listening to the proposal.
sentences.ja: 義務と訳すか強い推奨と訳すかで聞き手の反応が大幅に変わり得るため通訳者はためらった。

sentences.en: Instead of choosing whichever translation sounded most natural in the receiving language, she asked the speaker whether participants would actually be permitted to decline the proposed activity.
sentences.ja: 受け手の言語で最も自然な訳を選ぶのでなく、参加者は実際に活動を断れるのか発言者に尋ねた。

sentences.en: The speaker clarified that the activity was strongly encouraged but that exceptions would be necessary for people whose circumstances prevented them from participating.
sentences.ja: 強く推奨するが事情により参加できない人には例外が必要と発言者は明確にした。

sentences.en: Several listeners subsequently explained that they would have rejected the initial proposal if they had understood it to impose an unconditional requirement on every participant.
sentences.ja: 全員に無条件の要件を課すと理解していたら当初案に反対しただろうと後に数人が説明した。

sentences.en: The clarification therefore affected the substance of the international discussion rather than merely improving the choice of an individual word in the translated statement.
sentences.ja: したがって確認は訳文の一語を改善するだけでなく国際議論の内容自体に影響した。

sentences.en: The student organizers later considered how interpreters should respond when an apparently straightforward expression depends on assumptions that are not necessarily shared by speakers from different communities.
sentences.ja: 後に主催学生は一見単純な表現が異なる共同体の話者に必ずしも共有されない前提に依存するとき通訳者がどう対応すべきか考えた。

sentences.en: They recognized that asking for clarification on every possible difference could make a conversation extremely slow and might interrupt participants who were already expressing their ideas precisely enough for the immediate purpose.
sentences.ja: すべての相違について確認すると会話が極端に遅くなり当面の目的には十分正確に表現している参加者も中断し得ると認識した。

sentences.en: At the same time, avoiding questions altogether could create a misleading appearance of agreement when participants were actually attaching different meanings to an important condition of a proposal.
sentences.ja: 一方質問を全く避けると提案の重要条件に異なる意味を付しているにもかかわらず合意しているような誤った外観を生み得る。

sentences.en: The students therefore discussed giving interpreters permission to request clarification when an unresolved ambiguity could influence a consequential decision, rather than expecting them to conceal every moment of uncertainty.
sentences.ja: そこで重要判断に影響し得る曖昧さが未解決なら確認を求める許可を通訳者に与え、全ての不確かさを隠すよう期待しないことを議論した。

sentences.en: The team also prepared a short written summary of the decisions reached at the conference and invited participants to identify statements that did not match their understanding of the discussion.
sentences.ja: 会議での決定をまとめた短文も作り議論の理解と一致しない記述を挙げるよう参加者に求めた。

sentences.en: This additional procedure was intended to reveal significant discrepancies rather than establish that every utterance had been translated perfectly throughout the event.
sentences.ja: 追加手順は全発言が完全に訳されたと確定するのでなく重大な食い違いを明らかにする目的だった。

sentences.en: The organizers emphasized that their imagined experience did not provide evidence about the effectiveness of any actual professional interpreting method or accreditation standard.
sentences.ja: 架空の体験は実際の専門通訳手法や認定基準の有効性について根拠を提供しないと主催者は強調した。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the situation demonstrates a possible tension between the desire for fluent communication and the need to make unresolved differences in meaning visible to the people involved.
sentences.ja: それでも流暢な意思疎通への願いと未解決の意味の差を関係者に見えるようにする必要との緊張を示す。

sentences.en: International dialogue requires more than linguistic equivalence, because speakers may use similar expressions while imagining substantially different consequences for the actions they are discussing.
sentences.ja: 国際対話には言語的等価性以上が必要だ。同様の表現でも議論中の行動に全く異なる結果を想定し得るからだ。

sentences.en: A well-timed question can reveal a distinction that might otherwise remain hidden until participants attempt to implement an apparently shared decision.
sentences.ja: 適切な時点の質問は一見共有された判断を実施しようとするまで隠れ続けたかもしれない区別を示し得る。

sentences.en: The interpreter's contribution in this fictional example consists not only in providing words in another language but also in recognizing when the available words do not yet communicate a sufficiently definite meaning.
sentences.ja: この架空例での通訳者の貢献は別言語の語を提供するだけでなく利用可能な語が十分明確な意味を伝えていない時に気づくことでもある。

sentences.en: Cooperation becomes more robust when participants are able to clarify important assumptions before treating a smooth conversation as proof that meaningful agreement has already been achieved.
sentences.ja: 円滑な会話を実質的合意成立の証拠と扱う前に重要な前提を明確にできれば協力はより堅固になる。

vocabulary.definition: task one is expected to perform
differences between things expected to match

options: Choose the environmental projects for everyone.
Decide who could attend the conference.
Translate discussion between participants with different first languages.
She did not recognize the conference topic.
The translation could change the perceived force of the proposal.
She wanted to reject the proposal herself.
The speaker had already defined every condition.
questions.explanation_ja: 義務と推奨で反応が違う。

questions.prompt: What did she ask the speaker?
options: Whether participants could decline the activity.
Whether the conference would end early.
Whether she could change the project topic.

questions.prompt: Why did clarification affect the substance of discussion?
options: It established the exact duration of the meeting.
The distinction altered whether listeners would accept the proposal.
It guaranteed that every listener would agree.

questions.prompt: What problem could excessive clarification create?
options: It could needlessly interrupt a conversation.
It would prevent all ambiguity forever.
It would make every statement inaccurate.

questions.prompt: When should interpreters consider asking questions?
options: Whenever a speaker finishes a sentence.
Only after every decision is implemented.
When ambiguity could affect a consequential decision.
questions.explanation_ja: 重要判断に影響する場合。

options: Interpreters took a compulsory vocabulary test.
The discussion was repeated word for word.
Participants reviewed a written summary of decisions.

questions.prompt: Why not claim every utterance was perfectly interpreted?
options: The review aimed to reveal major discrepancies, not guarantee perfection.
The organizers knew every translation was inaccurate.
Translation should always proceed without questions.
Clarifying consequential differences in meaning can make international agreement more reliable.

paraphrases.source: The interpreter hesitated because translating the expression as an obligation rather than a strong recommendation might substantially alter the response of the people listening to the proposal.
paraphrases.rewrite: The speaker used an expression whose degree of obligation was unclear to the interpreter.

paraphrases.source: Several listeners subsequently explained that they would have rejected the initial proposal if they had understood it to impose an unconditional requirement on every participant.
paraphrases.rewrite: Some listeners would have opposed the proposal had it meant an absolute obligation.

paraphrases.source: The student organizers later considered how interpreters should respond when an apparently straightforward expression depends on assumptions that are not necessarily shared by speakers from different communities.
paraphrases.rewrite: The organizers ask how to respond when simple-looking language relies on unshared assumptions.

paraphrases.source: Cooperation becomes more robust when participants are able to clarify important assumptions before treating a smooth conversation as proof that meaningful agreement has already been achieved.
paraphrases.rewrite: Clarifying assumptions before assuming agreement strengthens cooperation.
